## OWNER-ADMITTED — Task 24 / Step 2 — Self-adoption qualification and implementation (2026-10-12)

**CORRECTION of the previous owner continuation entry:** The owner explicitly allocates a **new Step 2**, not another iteration of Step 1. Step 1 completed its investigation/result handoff in [PR #25](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/pull/25) at head `e091718b0b6eb8c2a64726174317bce69afd42d8` with the [canonical Step 1 Outcome](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/24#issuecomment-6120052165) and a bounded research-only exact-head assessment. The prior heading and instruction saying "same Step 1" were my mistaken interpretation; they are **superseded** by this Step 2 admission. Step 1 research evidence remains valid and auditable, but was neither a full native implementation nor merge/release approval.

The owner authorizes **Task 24 / Step 2** to conduct the targeted comparisons below, then implement, test and correct the smallest qualified solution end-to-end **within Step 2** as current scope allows. This lifts Step 1's stop-for-owner-decision boundary only for those bounded investigations and in-scope implementation. No choice has been made yet between a producer exception and widening scope to patch/upgrade VibeVM. Stop for another focused owner decision if the checks still establish an important unresolved policy or scope choice.

**Step/PR lifecycle:** Step 2 is a **distinct work unit** with its own current objective and attributable Step 2 Outcome, not a replay of Step 1. Reconcile the actual Git history, the open Step 1 research PR #25, and the valid research assessment before choosing the smallest safe Step 2 branch/PR update. This admission does **not** authorize merging PR #25, rewriting its history, discarding its evidence, or claiming its research assessment approves new implementation. Preserve original Task #24 rather than creating another task; do not impose an unqualified universal one-PR-per-Step rule or require a new PR merely because a Step number changed. Use the ordinary independent **exact-head review** boundary for the eventual Step 2 candidate.

**Recheck the Codex `AGENTS.md` loading problem with the smallest viable workflow:**
- Codex may automatically load candidate-checkout `AGENTS.md` **before** processing the user's task prompt; that alone does not mean it executed any command before seeing the prompt. Differentiate model guidance consistency from OS/sandbox security and hostile candidate-code containment.
- In a disposable actual supported **Manual Codex** launch, compare (a) a straightforward explicit task prompt binding an exact independently accepted source-`main` guidance SHA and treating candidate `AGENTS.md`, nested rules and generated boot as *test data only*, with (b) the previously tested accepted-snapshot `-C` / candidate `--add-dir` approach. Use harmless conflicting instruction markers; inspect inherited/root/nested routing, conditional reads, candidate edits, and feasible continuation/review use. Preserve existing host/client permission boundaries; do not modify global instructions or credentials.
- Assess whether the simple prompt approach is **sufficiently reliable for preventing accidental candidate-rule activation** in supported manual usage; do not falsely call it an enforceable isolation/security boundary or assert that user prompts outrank system/developer instructions. Prefer the least costly proven approach and disclose client-specific/unproven behavior.

**Recheck the real pinned VibeVM 1.0.7 dogfooding path, not just a different path-dependency fixture:**
- Reproduce the upstream root declaration `flow:org.vibevm.world/multi-user-planning` with `version = "^1.0.0"`, `link = "static-transitive"`, the versioned `vibevm/vibepacks/<group>/<name>/v<version>` source tree, and `vibe install --offline --registry <root>/vibevm/vibepacks`. Then adapt *that same supported pattern* to `flow:org.jresearch.ai/development-governance` in a disposable representation of our producer; compare to the earlier `{path=..., link="dynamic"}` tests.
- Explain **independently** the typed `flow:` identity, `^version` versus exact pin, TOML form, registry versus path resolution, `static-transitive` versus `dynamic` routing/JIT semantics, and upstream vs our source layout. Do not imply changing link mode fixes `ORDER-LAW` without evidence.
- Upstream's own checked-in `vibe.lock` contains absolute local `file://` URLs; measure the consequences for fresh clone, moving workspaces, re-install/update, provenance and committing materialization. Also qualify the prior Task 22 direct-Git source/update route *for this repo's real nested package layout*, and whether existing exporter/Git/CI checks can cover missing/corrupt slots without new framework code.
- Evaluate clean accepted-`main` checkout with ready-to-read committed source+projection, candidate materialization and exact-head review, pull/checkout/rollback, overlay preservation, and mismatch detection; keep evidence explicit about synthetic versus production probes.

**Step 2 execution / completion:** If a small native, portable, correct design meets the original acceptance and conditional-loading contract, implement + test + correct it and package the shared self-adoption protocol as the applicable new version in the **Step 2 reviewed candidate** (do not alter frozen releases). Remove the Task 22 helper only after the actual supported startup/adoption path is qualified. If an important choice or material extra operator work remains, report the remaining concrete gap and request a focused owner decision **after these comparisons**, rather than treating the earlier proposed exception or a VibeVM patch as already authorized. No unnecessary security theater, new approval ceremony or stand-alone manager. Revalidate the Step 2 result and publish a **separate Step 2 Outcome** linking the Step 1 Outcome; preserve historical comments and evidence.

**Boundaries unchanged:** no self-approval, merge, release, direct-to-main edits, consumer/Relay install, credentials, GitHub settings changes or Issue closure. Independent exact-head review remains necessary for the Step 2 result.

---

## Status and decision (2026-10-12)

**OWNER-ADMITTED — Task 24 / Step 1 / Shared self-adoption protocol (2026-10-12).** The owner authorizes one complete Manual Codex execution cycle to investigate, implement, test, correct and prepare one reviewable PR under the scope and boundaries below. This admission supersedes the previous NOT YET ADMITTED status; publish one exact-head Outcome and stop for independent review. Codex Relay-specific Writer, typed Request/Decision/CR and automation procedures do not apply. Create one coherent shared, conditional **self-adoption** protocol and qualify/reconcile this repository's implementation against it. This is the successor architectural investigation to completed [#22](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/22) / merged [PR #23](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/pull/23), not a reopening or retroactive rejection of its independently accepted result.

**Step 1 result handoff (2026-10-12):** [PR #25](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/pull/25), exact head `e091718b0b6eb8c2a64726174317bce69afd42d8`; [one canonical Outcome](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/24#issuecomment-6120052165). Investigation and a protocol design draft are reviewable. The preferred pinned native replacement is blocked by reproduced tool gaps; the existing implementation is preserved. Independent review and an explicit owner disposition are pending; implementation/packaging and Task completion are not claimed.

**Selected preferred design:** use ordinary VibeVM workspace/package materialization, **commit generated guidance/dependency/boot artifacts to Git in the same PR as the authored changes**, and ensure development/review uses rules from **accepted source `main`**, not the candidate branch. Aim for **one reviewed PR, no additional post-publication self-adoption PR, and a ready-to-use clean checkout**. Treat this as a design hypothesis requiring real Codex/VibeVM qualification, **not** proof that today's VibeVM 1.0.7 / Codex startup already implements it.

## Problem

Producer repositories may author guidance that governs their own development. A self-adoption solution must work repeatedly across projects rather than reinventing update scripts for each one:

- `shared-governance` publishes the Development Governance flow and itself adopts relevant shared protocols.
- `codex-relay` will publish version-compatible product guidance / native Codex Skill under [Relay #91](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/91), and may need to use its own accepted guidance during development; its executable runtime installation remains a different, separately authorized lifecycle.
- Other projects may produce their own reusable rules, documentation, or agent adapters.

Current #22 implementation uses `scripts/self-adopt.py` and an ignored `.vibe/accepted-governance` projection, selecting accepted **published** releases at effort start. Its standalone selection/reading checks passed, but the complete Codex startup -> helper -> guidance read was not end-to-end qualified. Re-evaluate whether this extra bespoke resolver/cache is justified now that a **general** self-adoption contract is intended.

## Shared conditional protocol — required semantics

1. **Applicability:** apply only where a producer itself consumes some of its own authored/published guidance or Skills; other repositories ignore the protocol. Keep one coherent `org.jresearch.ai/development-governance` flow package unless actual evidence triggers [#17](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/17).
2. **Authority:** normal development and independent review run under guidance from an identifiable, independently accepted **source `main` commit**, frozen for the current effort/review as appropriate. Acceptance of a source commit and subsequent public package publication are **distinct events**. A producer need not wait for its own public release to use independently accepted source, unless its local product contract explicitly requires publication. Downstream consumers retain their own explicit adoption/compatibility decisions.
3. **Candidates are not authority:** edits in a task/PR branch, including `vibe install` output, candidate `AGENTS.md` changes and generated boot/Skill projections, may be developed, materialized, diffed and tested, but **must not silently govern the producing Codex session or independent review of that same candidate**. Do not forbid `vibe install` in development branches: distinguish candidate artifacts from accepted active instructions.
4. **Prefer native tools:** use the host's supported standard package manager/materializer/installer (VibeVM for this producer, native Skill installer when appropriate elsewhere), not a prescribed custom Python resolver. Stable inputs, exact provenance, conditional/JIT routing, safe rollback and preserved project-local overlays. Avoid mandatory services, registries, global policy engines, update ledgers, arbitrary model gates or universal PR policy.
5. **Source-controlled ready state:** the supported producer layout should commit materialized dependencies and generated boot/agent routing **with source changes in the same PR**. A fresh clone/checkout of accepted `main` must contain functioning applicable guidance **without first running VibeVM, downloading anything, or executing a bootstrap script**. A later `git pull`/checkout must advance source and its committed projection together. CI detects missing, stale or conflicting generated outputs. Ordinary Codex execution only reads those accepted files; VibeVM runs during deliberate development/maintenance.
6. **Review boundary:** author and materialize candidates before requesting independent exact-head review; review includes source, generated diff, semantics, current accepted authority, and validation. If edits follow approval, revalidate and re-review the changed head. No need for a special GitHub “generate just before merge” hook or separate post-merge adoption PR.
7. **Tests of future rules:** structural checks and simple scenario walkthroughs by default. When behavior needs model qualification, use an **isolated disposable probe** fed the candidate guidance. This tests a candidate without promoting it to the main developer/reviewer session; no new persistent TEST environment or complex approval framework by default.
8. **Failure and recovery:** do not activate partial/corrupted results; detect producer/source/slot/index mismatches and preserve accepted guidance. Git revert/restore is the ordinary rollback for committed materialization. Do not treat a publication outage as revocation of an already independently accepted source change.

## Implementation investigation — concrete work in this repository

- Compare actual [VibeVM in-tree dogfooding](https://github.com/vibevm/vibevm/blob/main/vibe.toml), local-workspace resolution, checked-in `vibe.lock` / `vibevm/vibedeps` and boot projection with the current published-dependency option and #22's direct accepted-release projection. Specifically qualify **pinned VibeVM 1.0.7** and this repository's one-member workspace; earlier #22 work found local/path-only resolution limitations. Do not assume upstream behavior or portability without a clean-clone proof.
- **Resolve the critical Codex loading issue:** Codex normally discovers `AGENTS.md` in its current checkout, which can be the candidate branch. Merely writing “read `main`” into candidate-controlled prose is **not an enforceable trust boundary**. Test the actual supported manual Codex launch/handoff, inherited project instructions and VibeVM-managed blocks. Find the **smallest reliable** means to bind the working/review session to a concrete accepted-`main` guidance snapshot while allowing candidate files to be edited/tested. Separate accepted agent instruction authority from untrusted worktree artifacts. If this cannot be enforced with supported tools, provide clear evidence and a minimal alternative/owner decision before replacing the existing mechanism; never claim an unproven guarantee.
- Qualify `vibe install`/regeneration and committed projection from local source, avoiding machine-specific source paths, hidden cache assumptions and loss of human-authored `AGENTS.md` overlays. Verify candidate materialization cannot accidentally become active; verify an accepted merged source+projection is immediately usable on clean clone, and update/check/recovery behavior is deterministic and repeatable.
- If the preferred design is technically sound, replace `scripts/self-adopt.py`, ignored accepted-release cache routing and now-redundant baseline bookkeeping **with the smaller native implementation**. Reconcile root `AGENTS.md`, [self-adoption documentation](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/blob/main/docs/self-adoption.md), release/authoring instructions, CI and regression tests; preserve the already accepted semantic coverage and local bindings for `proportional-controls`, `requirement-authority`, `package-versioning`, `task-handoff`. Do not casually discard #22's verified behavior before its replacement is proven.
- Add a concise reusable ordinary **flow protocol** to Development Governance with conditional adoption/routing; apply the accepted package-versioning and source/export workflow to a **new** version, never mutate frozen published artifacts. Make the producer's own startup/use follow the new protocol only after independent acceptance. Generic contract belongs here; Relay-specific guidance and distribution belong under Relay [#91](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/91), with cross-project coordination under [#59](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/codex-relay/issues/59).

## Boundaries / validation

- **One admitted Manual Codex cycle — Task 24 / Step 1** may investigate, implement, test, correct and prepare one candidate PR; do not create a chain of research-only/implementation-only/TEST-only Tasks just to revisit the same design. Stop and request an owner decision if evidence invalidates the preferred design or requires widening authority.
- Verify at least: clean accepted-main clone, checkout switch/pull, candidate edited protocol + candidate `vibe install`, independent read of prior accepted rules during candidate development and review, correct generated diff/lock/boot, conditional protocol loading, no stale/missing projection, safe retry and Git rollback. Disclose unsupported operating/client environments and genuine upstream limitations.
- Preserve exact-head independent review and ordinary owner-authorized merge/release separation. No self-approval, no automatic merge, no direct-to-main mutation, no GitHub setting/protection change, no live consumer/Relay installation or Skill rollout, no credentials/deployment, and no publication by merely creating this Issue. Keep unrelated [#13](https://github.com/jresearchsoftware/shared-governance/issues/13) repository setup policy separate.
- No new standalone self-adoption manager/service unless a demonstrated tool gap makes it strictly necessary; prefer reducing code and ceremony over speculative hardening. Do not attempt to defend against arbitrary malicious candidate code with a prose-only rule.

## Completion

Independently accepted shared conditional protocol, qualified **source-controlled native self-adoption** in this producer or an explicit evidence-backed owner decision to retain/change the implementation, and a coherent clean-checkout/rollback path. One normal exact-head candidate review and separately authorized merge. Publication of a new package version follows the existing release workflow, not execution admission. Document any remaining native client/loader limits rather than declaring success without end-to-end proof.

**Task lifecycle:** open; Step 1 investigation published for independent review. Native implementation and protocol packaging are held for the explicit owner disposition required above; independent acceptance and owner-authorized closure remain pending.
title: Define shared self-adoption protocol and native accepted-main producer adoption
